newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy to try to raise refugee boat wreck - Albania.
newsitem.headline: Italy to try to raise refugee boat wreck - Albania.

text.p: Italy has told Albania that it will try to raise the wreck of a refugee boat that sank in the Adriatic following a collision with an Italian navy ship, Albanian Defence Minister Shaqir Vukaj said on Wednesday.

Vukaj, speaking in the southeast Italian port of Brindisi where he met some of the 34 survivors of last Friday's disaster, said Albania had asked Italy officially to salvage the wreck, which Tirana says could hold around 80 bodies.
He said Italian Defence Minister Beniamino Andreatta "has assured me that Italy will make every effort to meet this request".

The sinking soured relations between Rome and Tirana as Italy prepares to lead a multinational security force to chaotic Albania to assist in a humanitarian relief mission to the Balkan state, where rebels are in control of large areas of the south.
Italian Prime Minister Romano Prodi made a surprise visit on Wednesday to the southern town of Gjirokaster, flying in for brief talks with Albanian Prime Minister Bashkim Fino.

He was due to address parliament later on Wednesday on the sinking and the planned force deployment after meeting the visiting European mediator for Albania, former Austrian Chancellor Franz Vranitzky.
Military experts from countries willing to contribute to the force were also holding a first round of planning talks in Rome on Wednesday, Italian defence ministry sources said.

Friday's sinking entailed the first known loss of life since Italy began controversial naval interdiction patrols late last month after some 13,000 Albanians fled to Italian shores in an uncontrolled exodus from their country's armed upheaval.
The boat, which had set out from the rebel-held southern port of Vlore, sank in 800 metres of water after a collision with the navy corvette Sibilla.
Tirana says at least 80 people drowned. Many of the 34 survivors have accused the Italians of ramming their ship, charges Italy denies.
Vukaj was accompanied to Brindisi by Italian deputy defence minister Massimo Brutti and navy chief of staff Admiral Angelo Mariani.
Flags on Italian and Albanian boats in Brindisi harbour, the main point of arrival in the recent refugee influx, flew at half mast in memory of the dead.
